_stage2c_launch.splash_repairs: BOTH splashes were repaired rather than merely preserved. Neither could be dismissed by Escape; Lumina's closed TWICE on Enter or Space (a keydown handler calling .click() on top of native activation, measured as 2 clicks and two 'Welcome home' toasts); neither returned focus into the app, leaving it on <body>; and in both games the world keydown handler was live BEHIND the splash, so r/w/p/Backspace mutated and persisted state before the player had started. All now route through one splashClosed truth with a capture-phase handler that removes itself.

_sports_rail_ruling_2026_08_07.supersedes: The Stage 2C reading, recorded in _stage2c_launch.sports_rail, that the rail was the Apex series and Aurora Links 3D therefore belonged off it. That was written down as a question precisely so it could be answered; it has been, and the answer is the opposite of the provisional reading.

gates_moved_and_why.CONVERTED (stale pin): verify_2c_shelf.js asserted Aurora was OFF the rail via `sports.every(t => /^Apex /.test(t))`. That clause encodes the premise the ruling overturned and would have hard-failed on any genuine non-Apex member forever. Not deleted and not weakened — it now guards the ruling, so it still goes red if Aurora is quietly dropped. Its tamper was inverted to match.
gates_moved_and_why.NOT CONVERTED (gate was correct): verify_sports_rail.js S5 went red on 'rail members share an icon'. S5 checks icons WITHIN the rail; Aurora and Apex Golf both carried the golf flag, which cost nothing on separate rails and became the rail's first intra-rail collision the moment the sixth member landed. The CONTENT moved, not the gate.
gates_moved_and_why.UNTOUCHED: S1-S4 and S6 of verify_sports_rail.js derived the six and passed with no edits. That file's header already promised 'adding a sixth sports game should make this gate check more, not go red', and it kept the promise.
gates_moved_and_why.ADDED: S7, a two-way membership control: drop a member (6 -> 5 derived) and invent a phantom seventh (rejected as an incomplete catalogue entry). Added because the rail gained its first non-Apex member and a one-directional membership check would watch a game fall off the rail without noticing.

_hearth_feel_finding_2026_08_07.ruling: Matt, 2026-08-07: the hearth "isn't quite a fireplace". A FEEL finding, not a strobe complaint — the ~2.7Hz measurement was inside the 3Hz rule and stayed inside it.
_hearth_feel_finding_2026_08_07.what_it_actually_was: The brief expected the Hearth palette's ambient/glow to be modulated alongside the flames. IT WAS NOT — there was no ambient modulation anywhere, and nothing in the room was driven by `time`. The entire hearth was one line: flick = .8 + sin(time*8)*.12 + sin(time*17)*.08, a uniform scale on two flame beziers. 8 and 17 are coprime integers, so the pattern repeated EXACTLY every 2pi seconds. That is why it read as a lamp on a timer, and the fire lit nothing but itself.
_hearth_feel_finding_2026_08_07.change: feel finding: regular pulse -> layered irregular flicker. Value noise over three incommensurate octaves, asymmetric one-pole (quick catch, slow fall), slow envelope allowing near-still lulls. Flames, embers, ceiling glow and window warmth all read the SAME source; the room's share runs through a slower follower.

numbers_before_after.reduced motion: 0 moving pixels both builds — genuinely static warm glow, OS-as-floor and the live listener untouched

_hearth_feel_finding_2026_08_07.tuning_error_worth_keeping: The first re-authoring measured 0.32 peaks/sec with peak-to-peak 0.55 over NINETY seconds, which looked healthy. Plotted over the four seconds a person actually watches it was almost a flat line. A summary statistic over a long window hid that nothing moved in any window anyone would see. The gain is now set so the WORST four-second stretch travels 0.23 of the flame's scale, against 0.38 for the old build.
_hearth_feel_finding_2026_08_07.instrument: tools/measure_hearth_flicker.mjs, one instrument run on both builds, with --self-test proving it recovers 2.706Hz, 1.273Hz and 0 from known inputs at two scales. It took four wrong versions — absolute peak tolerance, no settle, a locus that spanned the wrong object, and no guard against the game's 10s forage respawn desynchronising the two comparison passes.
_hearth_feel_finding_2026_08_07.noted_not_fixed: The 2C harness's L4b measures world progress per unit of WALL time, so it is sensitive to render cost. Observed 0.902, 0.947, 1.008 and 1.143 across runs against a +/-10% band. It passes but will flake; the defect it targets sits at 0.400, so the band could be one-sided without losing anything.
_hearth_feel_finding_2026_08_07.frames: six before/after pairs across 4s plus the flame-scale trace — /tmp/hearth-frames/hearth-before-after.png
